extracted.intended_audience: members of the public requesting records and agency FOIA/Privacy Act officers at the President's Commission on White House Fellowships and the National Capital Planning Commission
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing how individuals may request, access, correct, and obtain agency records under the Privacy Act and the Freedom of Information Act for the National Capital Planning Commission (and related Presidential Commission provisions). Covers identification, timelines, fees, disclosures, appeals, and fee-waiver criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement and existence-notification timelines (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will acknowledge requests for the existence of records within 10 working days from the time it receives the request and will normally notify the requester of the existence or non-existence of records within 30 working days from receipt of request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for requests for access (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may request review of records pertaining to him by appearing at Room 1308, 1900 E Street, NW., Washington, DC on work days between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m. or by writing to the Commission Administrative Officer. The Commission will strive either to make the record available within 15 working days of the request or to inform the requester of the need for additional identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appearing in person reasonable identification (employment ID, driver's license, or credit cards) will normally be accepted in absence of contrary indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity verification for existence inquiries (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: No special identity verification is required for individuals who wish to know whether a specific system of records pertains to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy fees and remittance rules (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges for copies of records will be at the rate of $0.10 per photocopy of each page. No charge will be made unless the charge as computed would exceed $3 for each request or related series of requests. If a fee in excess of $25 would be required, the requester shall be notified and the fee must be tendered before the records will be copied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remittances must be personal check or bank draft drawn on a U.S. bank or a money order payable to the Treasury of the United States and mailed or delivered to the Administrative Officer at the Commission address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right not to be denied access (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals will not be denied access to records pertaining to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting correction or amendment (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may request that a record or records pertaining to him or her be amended or corrected. Such requests shall be submitted in writing to the Administrative Officer at the Commission’s business address. The signature of the requester will be sufficient identification for requesting correction of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request must contain an exact description of the item(s) sought to be amended, specific reasons for the requested amendment, and the individual's birthdate for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines and notice for correction requests (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 working days after receipt of a request to amend a record, the Administrative Officer shall transmit a written acknowledgement of receipt. Requester will be notified within 30 days whether his or her request has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No acknowledgement is required if the request can be reviewed and processed with notification of compliance or denial within the ten-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive criteria for amending records (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Administrative Officer shall determine a requested amendment is appropriate to ensure the record is: (1) relevant and necessary to accomplish the purposes for which the records were collected; and (2) as accurate, timely, and complete as are reasonably necessary to assure fairness to the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appropriate, the agency shall change the record, advise the requester that the change has been made (thirty days from receipt of written request), and—after an accounting of disclosures—advise previous recipients who still retain a copy of the amendment and its substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of amendment and administrative review rights (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Administrative Officer determines the requested amendment is not in conformity with the Act, he shall advise the requester in writing within 30 days with specific reasons and inform the requester that further review by the Director is available if requested in writing within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director must make an independent review within 30 working days using the amendment criteria; if Director denies, requester may file a concise statement of disagreement that will be annotated to the record and made available to subsequent recipients; prior recipients believed to still retain a copy will be sent the statement after an accounting of disclosures; the requester is informed of right to seek judicial review (5 U.S.C. 552a(g)(1)(A)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of records to persons other than subject (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records subject to the Privacy Act that are requested by any person other than the individual to whom they pertain will not be made available except under specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted disclosure example: records may be circulated to appropriate officials incident to placing Fellows in work assignments. An accounting of date, nature, purpose, and recipient of each disclosure will be indicated on the record and is available to the individual on written request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope statement (NCPC Privacy Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: These procedures provide the means by which individuals may safeguard their privacy by obtaining access to, and requesting amendments or corrections in, information about these individuals which is under the control of the National Capital Planning Commission (the 'Commission').

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act definitions (NCPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions provided include: (a) 'individual' (U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident); (b) 'maintain' includes maintain, collect, use, or disseminate; (c) 'record' means any item or grouping of information about an individual that is maintained and contains the individual's name or identifying particular; (d) 'system of records' means a group of records from which information is retrieved by name or identifier; (e) 'routine use' means a purpose compatible with the purpose for which it was collected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for determining whether a record exists (NCPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual who wishes to know whether a system of records maintained by the Commission contains a record pertaining to him or her shall submit a written request to the appropriate System Manager. The System Manager shall, within 10 days of receipt, inform the individual whether a system of records contains such a record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access request options and identification (NCPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual who desires access to any identified record shall file a request addressed to the System Manager indicating whether the individual intends to appear in person at the Commission’s offices or desires to receive a copy by mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-person: present identification (valid driver’s license or employee identification card) to permit verification. Mail delivery: include date and location of birth as suitable proof of identity. Where those forms are not feasible, the Commission may request a signed statement asserting identity and noting criminal penalties for false pretenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure to individual upon verification (NCPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon verification of identity, the System Manager shall disclose to the individual: (a) the information contained in the record that pertains to that individual; and (b) the accounting of disclosures required by 5 U.S.C. 552a(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency review of correction requests and appeal (NCPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within ten days of receipt of a request to correct or amend the record, the System Manager will acknowledge receipt and promptly either (a) make any correction or amendment and inform the individual, or (b) inform the individual of refusal, reasons, and procedures to request review. An individual may appeal a refusal to the Chairman, who will complete review within 30 days (unless extended for good cause). If the Chairman also refuses, the individual may file a concise statement of disagreement and seek judicial review under 5 U.S.C. 552a(g)(1)(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompaniment for in-person disclosure (NCPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual to whom a record is to be disclosed in person may have a person of his or her choosing accompany the individual when the record is disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for Privacy Act requests (NCPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will not charge an individual for costs of searching for a record or reviewing the record. When the Commission makes a copy of a record as a necessary part of disclosure, the Commission will not charge for making that copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an individual requests a copy of the record when a copy has not otherwise been made as necessary to disclose, the Commission will charge $0.25 per page (maximum page dimension specified) to the extent that the request exceeds $5.00 in cost to the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA general policy (NCPC FOIA regulations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's general policy is to facilitate the broadest possible availability and dissemination of information to the public. Staff is available to assist the public formally via procedures herein or informally by discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To the extent permitted by other laws, the Commission will make available records which it is authorized to withhold when it determines disclosure is in the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place of obtaining information and routing (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information may be obtained only from the Commission's offices at 1325 G Street, NW. Requests for publications or general information should be directed to the Public Affairs Officer; all formal FOIA requests must be directed to the Freedom of Information Officer. Any request directed initially to the wrong source will be routed correctly and the requester notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ten-day time period for determining whether to comply with a request does not begin until the request reaches, or with due diligence should have reached, the appropriate information source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of information routinely available (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following types of information shall be routinely available (subject to fee schedule and FOIA exemptions): (1) correspondence between the Commission and the public; (2) Executive Director's Recommendations; (3) Committee Reports; (4) Commission Memorandums of Actions; and (5) Maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map requests directed to Public Affairs Officer; other requests to the Freedom of Information Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal FOIA request content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All formal requests under the Act shall be made in writing to the Freedom of Information Officer. To expedite handling 'Freedom of Information Request' should appear on the envelope. The request shall state it is made pursuant to the Act; shall reasonably describe the information sought (including date received/produced if known); shall state the maximum fee the requester is willing to pay; and should provide a telephone number.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOI Officer response timeline and unusual circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The Freedom of Information Officer shall determine within ten days after receipt whether to comply and immediately notify the requester and inform of right to appeal. The ten-day period may be extended by written notice for unusual circumstances, but not by more than ten working days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unusual circumstances means, to extent reasonably necessary: (1) need to search for and collect records from establishments separate from Commission offices; (2) need to search for, collect, and examine a voluminous amount of separate and distinct records demanded in a single request; (3) need for consultation with another agency with substantial interest or among two or more components of the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant determination notice content (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the FOI Officer grants a request in whole or part, notice will be in writing and include a description of the information to be made available, a statement of time and place for inspection or procedure for duplication and delivery, and a statement of the total fees chargeable pursuant to the fee schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial determination and appeal (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the FOI Officer denies a request in whole or part, he shall notify the requester in writing. Any appeal shall be made in writing to the Chairman, include a brief statement of legal/factual grounds for objection, and the Chairman shall decide within twenty days (excepting weekends and legal holidays) and provide written notice including a brief statement of reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of procedures for public-interest disclosure (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a waiver of any procedures would further the purpose of the Act by causing public disclosure of non-confidential information within the time period required, the FOI Officer may, in the context of individual requests, waive procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA schedule of fees and rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may charge fees for production of information: publications offered for sale as marked; Commission reports, committee reports, memorandums of actions, transcripts, and other records at $0.25/page; map publications (microfilm printout $1.00 each; ozalid maps $0.30/linear foot); manual record research $2.25 per quarter hour (clerical) or $5.00 per quarter hour (professional/managerial); review charges $5.00 per quarter hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may charge for search and review costs where applicable even if there is ultimately no disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester classifications and fee rules (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees may be applied based on requester classification: (i) Commercial use requester: may be charged all direct costs of searching, reviewing, and duplicating; (ii) Educational and non-commercial scientific institutions: documents provided for cost of reproduction alone, excluding charges for first 100 pages; (iii) Representatives of news media: reproduction cost alone, excluding first 100 pages; (iv) All other requesters: may be charged fees to recover full reasonable direct costs of searching and reproducing responsive records, excluding first 100 pages and first two hours of search time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests from record subjects for records about themselves continue to be treated under the Privacy Act fee provisions which permit fees only for reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited supply/back-copies policy (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission keeps a limited quantity of back copies of Executive Director's Recommendations, Committee Reports, and Commission Memorandums of Actions. It will first attempt to fill requests from its supply and until supply is exhausted will provide these documents at no charge. Once the supply is exhausted, documents will be provided in accord with the fee schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum fee and fee-collection economy rule (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may not charge fees if the cost of collecting the fee would be equal to or greater than the fee itself. The minimum fee for production of information will be $2.00 (over and above the first free 100 pages and 2 hours search time, where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee waiver/reduction substantive criteria (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FOI Officer shall provide documents without charge or at a reduced charge if disclosure is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of government operations or activities and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors to consider in deciding a waiver: (i) subject concerns operations/activities of Government; (ii) informative value of information to be disclosed; (iii) contribution to public understanding by the general public; (iv) significance of the contribution; (v) existence and magnitude of commercial interest; (vi) whether the requester's commercial interest is sufficiently large relative to public interest such that disclosure is primarily in the commercial interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approval / advance deposit of fees (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the agency estimates duplication, review or search charges are likely to exceed $25, it shall notify the requester of the estimated fees unless the requester has already indicated willingness to pay that amount. If fees anticipated are substantially greater than estimated in the request, the requester shall be immediately notified and afforded the opportunity to revise the request to reduce fees.
